children: Export sales of U.S. grains for the week landed within analyst forecasts, according to data from the Department of Agriculture.

In its weekly export sales report published Thursday, the USDA said that corn sales across the 2025/26 and 2026/27 marketing years totaled 1.16 million metric tons for the week ended August 27 - which included net sales reductions of 829,600 tons for 2025/26.
Soybean sales across 2025/26 and 2026/27 totaled 1.85 million tons, including net sales reductions of 94,200 tons. Wheat sales in 2026/27 totaled 313,500 tons.

Totals for all three row crops landed within the forecasts of analysts surveyed by The Wall Street Journal this week. This report covers the last full week of the 2025/26 marketing year, with the crop years for corn and soybeans rolling over September 1.
CBOT grain futures are lower in pre-market trading, with most-active corn futures down 2.3%, soybeans down 0.9%, and wheat dropping 4%.
To see related data, search "U.S. Export Sales: Weekly Sales Totals" in Dow Jones NewsPlus.
